newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - July 2.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Wednesday:

* The Congressional Budget Office has issued estimates suggesting that health-care measures passed last week by the U.S. House and Senate would not meet their stated aim of guaranteeing coverage for half of the nation's uninsured children.
* Environmentalists, long the electoral domain of Democrats, are now being courted by Republicans.
* As Mexican voters prepare to head to the polls on Sunday, the country's ruling party is facing the prospect of big losses.
* Hong Kong's new leader, Tung Chee-hwa, outlined his vision for the territory, now under Chinese rule.

* Boxer Mike Tyson's bite out of the ear of his opponent, Evander Holyfield, has stirred conflicting emotions in his old neighborhood, the Brownsville section of New York's Brooklyn borough. What he did was wrong, but he remains a hero on these mean streets.
* Beaches along Long Island Sound have been closed just as the beach season is about to officially open on the Independence Day holiday because of sewage that has seeped into the waters.
